summary:
This was a solo project where I researched the conditions on Mars and the Moon drawing from surface regolith, atmospheric conditions, temperature, gravity and more to find the most reminiscent regions on Earth naturally. I've listed each location and each factor contributed to a comprehensive summary linked below. 
It's essential to be able to understand not only the surface of these celestial bodies for exploration, but to know our limits in infrastructure and composition so we can rectify our error and adapt to the eventual future.
details:
My project organizes and classifies main locations on the Moon and Mars and carefully lists terrestrial locations that match certain aspects of both specific locations and general conditions on the surface of each. It may not be news, but the document has organizational value that helps communicate specifics to younger or less-experienced audiences. The intended impact of this project is to do just that. I may not be a great programmer, but I hope to be able to help someone with this data collected.

I first considered the general surface conditions on each body individually, then I zoned in on conditions of specific scientific interest typically containing things such as water ice, high volcanic activity, minerals or discovery. I then mapped each location out in a picture format using NASA's solar system treks and GeoHack to locate and point out each on a map. Next, I listed the main conditions out and found locations on Earth that closely match. I considered mainly atmospheric conditions, temperature, regolith and elevation for construction and survival.

If I had more time I would've gone into further detail, unfortunately I've been utterly busy.
